variants.asks: a source is a thing with a history. What does it mean to read one at a particular time?

steps.because: the rules, read as a line: every rule of the theory is a term, the reading having run each rule's program on a symbolic match and counted what it does to the population - what it makes, what it takes, what it carries, what a body puts in - so the line is what the rules come to as a crowd rather than a description of them. Everything a theorem of this theory stands on is a term of this line or a reading of one, so every premise below is read off it, and every derivation passes through it

derivation.because: ANNIHILATION contributes it: its body comes to -2 rays and -1 points of space, its quantifier makes it of degree 2 in the density across an edge, which is the facing factor, and its gates let through what they let through

rule /1 "Annihilation" | σ (x: 1 Edge{active}) => x.ANNIHILATE - -2 rays, -1 points of space. The reading follows the body down through the methods it calls, and the ledgers it moves are counted off the assignments it makes

the rule is quantified over 2 population-bearing refs, so its term carries the density to the power 2 - and the two are across an edge, so the rate goes against the oncoming current, which is the facing factor F
the rule fires only where active, so whatever it does it does on that share of its matches and the term carries it

steps.because: the local source l', read at a particular point in time, @t: its mass then - what it lit then, its \beta then - and nothing about it now. The mark is on the source, not on the equation: a source is a thing with a history, and @t picks one tick of it. What is read at that tick is the source's own line - the choice it makes over its ways. In the record every mass leaves at a local, each source is read at the tick the rays that reach the local left it, which is l.distance\paren{l'} ticks before now; that is where the sum uses the mark, and it is the only place a tick is picked for it
